match_note: Communications Materials file; R2's first-round report is also attached at the end. Version 0 comments match arXiv v1: v1 abstract says 'chemically undoped' and 'indicating that both materials support a three-dimensional antiferromagnetic order', contains the stripe-order sentence, the 'markedly different degree of out-of-plane hybridization' sentence, the H=0.4-0.475 averaged spectrum, 'almost pure' crossed character, and '0.7 eV peak, which is fully unpolarized ... [12]'. The orbital-dispersion model change, new U/Delta and SI figures S2-S6 came after v1.

concerns.quote: The manuscript does not provide adequate evidence for this conclusion. I assume this stems from incorrectly conflating nonzero interlayer magnetic exchange with magnetic order.
concerns.summary: Claims that PrNiO2 has 3D antiferromagnetic order are unsupported; interlayer exchange is not order.

concerns.quote: The claim that the nickelate is "chemically undoped" is likely not appropriate. There is extensive evidence that this material class often contains excess oxygen.
concerns.summary: Excess oxygen could act as an effective dopant, so 'chemically undoped' is not justified.

concerns.quote: this peak appears larger in samples showing stronger impurity-phase diffraction ... suggesting a possible extrinsic origin.
concerns.summary: The rare-earth 5d assignment of the 0.7 eV feature is not compelling; it may be extrinsic (impurity phases).

concerns.quote: It is unclear whether one can genuinely fit the 3z^2-r^2 energy in the nickelate, since none of the spectra show a local maximum at the asserted energy.
concerns.summary: The 3z2-r2 energy cannot be reliably fitted; fit description and parameter correlations are missing.

concerns.quote: The magnetic dispersion appears over-fit, in the sense that the model uses more free parameters than can plausibly be uniquely constrained.
concerns.summary: The magnon fit has too many free parameters; covariance and cross-correlations should show uniqueness.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: This sentence should be revised to present a more balanced and better referenced summary of the literature.
concerns.summary: The claim of a markedly different out-of-plane hybridization from rare-earth ions overstates one side of the literature, given similar J_perp values.

concerns.quote: speculative statements to explain this aspect of the data are unnecessary.
concerns.summary: Speculation about stripe order and 2D symmetry breaking to explain the asymmetric dispersion should be removed for a doped, unordered nickelate.

concerns.quote: to be confident that a genuine dispersion is present, rather than an apparent shift caused by differing contributions of nondispersive peaks.
concerns.summary: The apparent magnon dispersion could arise from varying weights of nondispersive peaks; line cuts with all fits and elastic assignment are needed.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: A significant problem with the current manuscript is that the model appears to selectively ignore pieces of evidence depending on what is most convenient.
concerns.summary: Model parameters (hopping, Delta, U) are selectively taken from the literature; the large Delta is inconsistent with sizable exchange and U should come from a d-p model.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Overall, the observations and conclusions are not focused/novel for publication in Communication Materials.
concerns.summary: Magnetic dispersions were reported before and many peculiarities were already observed, so novelty and focus are insufficient.

concerns.quote: The justification of this averaging is unclear
concerns.summary: The Fig. 2(a) spectrum averages over H=0.4-0.475 where the magnon disperses by ~20 meV.

concerns.quote: the experimental data do not justify the presence/absence of a magnon gap and thus the need for the reconsideration of the exchanges.
concerns.summary: The magnon gap at (0,0), and hence out-of-plane exchange, is not justified given large low-q error bars; low-q fits and intensity correlations are needed.

concerns.quote: such an argument can be made after the comparison with a non-SC d9 nickelate having long range AFM order
concerns.summary: Interpreting magnon damping as weak disruption of AFM order needs comparison with an ordered non-SC d9 nickelate; CCO resolution-limited width is unclear in Fig. 3(b).

concerns.quote: Detailed parameters for the single-ion calculations should be provided in the supplementary materials
concerns.summary: Single-ion calculation parameters (broadenings, spin direction) are not given.

concerns.quote: the single ion calculations which do not consider the hybridization match the polarization resolved data for PNO quite well
concerns.summary: The dxy polarization analysis overstates CCO purity, and the Pr 5d hybridization explanation for PNO is inconsistent with single-ion agreement in most geometries.

concerns.quote: This may be restated considering the 80% strength of in-plane hopping used for describing the orbital dispersion.
concerns.summary: The statement that in-plane hopping is similar to cuprates conflicts with the 80% hopping used later.

concerns.quote: Judging from Fig 4a-c, the statistics of PNO polarization analysis are too poor to make such a definite statement due to lack of intensity.
concerns.summary: The claim that the 0.7 eV peak is fully unpolarized is not supported by the noisy polarimetry data.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The mode energy does not track the highest intensity, especially near the gamma point.
concerns.summary: In Fig. 5c the assigned orbital mode energy does not follow the intensity maximum; the peak-position procedure is unclear.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: It would be worth mentioning that the in-plane strain for PNO and CCO are different.
concerns.summary: Different epitaxial strain in PNO and CCO should be discussed.

concerns.quote: It would be better to clarify whether the data present in this manuscript is the re-analysis of the same raw dataset
concerns.summary: Clarify whether CCO data are a reanalysis of previously published data or new measurements.

concerns.quote: Such peak has been theoretically assigned to Ni 3d-rare earth 5d hybridized states [12] ...", should the reference be [11]?
concerns.summary: Possible wrong citation for the 0.7 eV peak assignment.

concerns.quote: Note, there is a similar preprint on highly similar topic on arxiv 2511.09460.
concerns.summary: A closely related preprint exists.

later_concerns.quote: the abstract of the PDF I have still says ``indicating that both materials support a three-dimensional antiferromagnetic order.''
later_concerns.summary: The abstract still claims 3D antiferromagnetic order.

later_concerns.quote: What I am questioning is whether one can really fit this feature with a precision of order 10--20 meV.
later_concerns.summary: The 3z2-r2 fit precision is doubtful; report parameter correlation coefficients instead of Fig. S3.

later_concerns.quote: claiming out-of-plane exchanges with precision such as 5.9+-1.1 meV is too strong.
later_concerns.summary: J_perp precision is overstated given low-q fit uncertainties; a range or upper bound should be given.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
